status: Draft written for the app. The owner revises it after the pilot (§7.3 step 1) and bumps the version.
intro: Each item is a **state** (a short text or JSON record) and a **question** with options. Decide whether the state lets you answer the question with one of the options. If it does, press **Space** (answerable) and Enter. If it doesn't, tick every **abstain reason** that applies (1-0) and mark the words that show it. Judge from the state only: never use what you know about the world. Tick a reason only when you could point at what makes it true.
spans: Select words in the state (or in an option's description) and give them a role: **support** (backs an option), **refute** (rules an option out), **unsupported** (an option-side claim the state doesn't back), **framing** (hedges, attributions, quotes, conditionals). Link each span to the reasons it shows. Spans snap to whole words; hold Alt for exact characters.

positive.state: The council approved a new cycle lane on Mill Road, to open in spring.
positive.question: Did the striker score in Saturday's match?
positive.why: The state is about a cycle lane; the question is about football. Nothing in it is even on topic.

negative.state: The club confirmed the striker was injured in training on Friday and missed Saturday's match.
negative.question: Did the striker score in Saturday's match?
negative.why: On topic and it settles the question: a player who missed the match didn't score. Topicality is not the issue.

positive.state: The striker started Saturday's match and was substituted in the 70th minute.
positive.question: Did the striker score in Saturday's match?
positive.why: On topic, but nothing says whether he scored.

negative.state: The striker started Saturday's match and was substituted in the 70th minute after scoring twice.
negative.question: Did the striker score in Saturday's match?
negative.why: The state settles it. Don't tick not_enough_info because the state is short.

positive.state: The report lists the server as patched on 3 May. The appendix table shows the same server unpatched at the end of May.
positive.question: Was the server patched in May?
positive.why: One part supports 'true', another refutes it. Mark a support span and a refute span on the same option ('true').

negative.state: The server was unpatched on 1 May and patched on 3 May.
negative.question: Was the server patched in May?
negative.why: A change over time is not a conflict: both facts are consistent and the answer is yes.

positive.state: A spokesperson said the factory would probably close by June.
positive.question: Will the factory close by June?
positive.why: The only support is attributed and hedged ('a spokesperson said', 'probably'). Mark the framing span and the support span.

negative.state: The factory will not close by June, the company confirmed in its filing.
negative.question: Will the factory close by June?
negative.why: Negation is not hedging: a negated fact is a refutation. The filing settles it.

positive.state: As of March 2019, the bridge was closed for repairs.
positive.question: Is the bridge open? (as of the item's date)
positive.why: The state is dated and describes something that may have changed by the as-of date. Mark the dated phrase. Judge whether it could have changed, not whether it did.

negative.question: Was the bridge built before 1950?
negative.why: A date alone doesn't make a state stale: when a bridge was built can't change.

positive.state: The driver met the guard at the station. She was carrying a red bag.
positive.question: Was the driver carrying a red bag?
positive.why: 'She' can be read two ways, and the readings give different answers. Say which readings in the note.

negative.state: The driver met the guard at the station. The driver was carrying a red bag.
negative.question: Was the driver carrying a red bag?
negative.why: Only one reading is plausible. Don't tick ambiguous for far-fetched readings.

positive.state: Sales rose 4% in the first quarter.
positive.question: Did sales rise more than the competitor's?
positive.why: The question needs a parameter it doesn't give: which competitor.

negative.state: Sales rose 4% in the first quarter; the competitor's rose 2%.
negative.question: Did sales rise more than the competitor's?
negative.why: The parameter is fixed by context. Underspecified is about the question, not about missing facts (that is not_enough_info).

positive.state: The museum has been closed since 2020 and has no exhibitions.
positive.question: Which artist does the museum's current exhibition feature?
positive.why: The question presupposes a current exhibition; the state contradicts that. Mark the contradicting span (refute).

negative.question: Which artist does the museum's current exhibition feature?
negative.why: The state doesn't contradict the presupposition, it just doesn't say. Judge the premise against the state only.

positive.state: The meeting was moved to Thursday.
positive.question: On which day is the meeting? Options: a) Monday b) Tuesday c) Wednesday
positive.why: The state settles the matter (Thursday), but no option says so.

negative.state: The meeting was moved from Monday.
negative.question: On which day is the meeting? Options: a) Monday b) Tuesday c) Wednesday
negative.why: The state doesn't settle which day; that is not the same as settling it outside the options.

positive.state: The new menu has twelve dishes, four of them vegetarian.
positive.question: Is the new menu good?
positive.why: The answer depends on taste, not on the state. Say why in the note if the batch asks for one.

negative.state: The new menu has twelve dishes, four of them vegetarian.
negative.question: Does the new menu have more than ten dishes?
negative.why: A count is a fact. Evaluative words in the state ('good', 'popular') don't make the question subjective either.
